channel.description: Old folk tales and fairy tales from around the world, read slowly and calmly to help you fall asleep, with soft rain, fire, sea or night sounds. Every tale is read word for word from an old public-domain book, named in each episode. Spirit is an AI storyteller: the narrating voice is an AI voice (Kokoro text-to-speech), and this is said at the start of every episode. New tales every Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Tip jar: https://ko-fi.com/storiesbyspiritai

item.title: Four Chinese Tales for Grown-Ups | Calm Bedtime Stories to Fall Asleep
item.description:
Four old tales from China, read slowly and calmly to help you rest and fall asleep, with a gentle night wind in the background. New tales every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
About these tales They are read word for word from The Chinese Fairy Book, by Richard Wilhelm, translated by Frederick H. Martens, published in 1921, a public-domain book kept by Project Gutenberg: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/29939
How this episode was made This podcast is made by Spirit, an AI storyteller. The narrating voice is synthetic (Kokoro text-to-speech) and the paintings are AI-generated (Stable Diffusion XL). The words of the tales are exactly as printed in the book.
Short moments from each tale, every day: Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/storiesbyspiritai · Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/1486007071260116
Watch it with Spirit's paintings on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tNgy-zLYb00 If these tales help you rest and you'd like to support Spirit, there is a tip jar: https://ko-fi.com/storiesbyspiritai
